correctness.rationale: Orthogonal diagonalization reduces the SPD system to independent scalar modes. For each mode the exact state matrix has trace \(1+\alpha-q[1+\lambda(1-\alpha)]\) and determinant \(\alpha(1-q)\). The three quadratic Schur inequalities reduce to two automatic positive terms and the single sharp bound \(q<2(1+\alpha)/[(1+\alpha)+\lambda(1-\alpha)]\). At equality \(-1\) is exactly a root. The verifier independently replays these identities and randomized boundary tests.

originality.rationale: The defining Grokfast paper gives the EMA gradient amplifier, its frequency response, hyperparameter ranges, and equivalence results for linear optimizers, but its inspected full text contains no quadratic, eigenvalue, Schur-stability, or learning-rate-bound analysis. Focused semantic database searches returned only stability results for different methods. The new statement links the source filter directly to an exact Nyquist-gain stability ceiling.
residual_risks: A similar closed-loop calculation may exist in unindexed control-oriented notes on gradient filtering.

The stability result does not establish or explain grokking itself.

value.rationale: Grokfast is explicitly designed as a frequency-selective gradient amplifier, and its source tunes \(\alpha\) and \(\lambda\) by cutoff frequency. The exact learning-rate ceiling therefore answers a natural safety question for the defining mechanism. The Nyquist identity explains why the source defaults can provide threefold DC amplification with little loss of quadratic stability, while another point inside the recommended range loses over one third of the vanilla margin. This is a structural design rule rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
